text:
Nick Suzuki missed a stretch of games and came back on Nov. 5 with a goal and two assists in an overtime win over Utah. Fifteen points in 11 games is a captain playing like last season's Selke Trophy winner, which he is.

How much of it is real? Most of it. His own chances are strong (4.6 expected goals) and Montreal controls 58% of expected goals at 5-on-5 with him out there. The soft spot is the finishing around him: the Canadiens have scored 5.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. Evolving-Hockey had him 4th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement in 2025-26, though they note his results ran ahead of his chances that year too.

Andrew Berkshire of Game Over Network pointed out the odd part: with Suzuki in the lineup, Montreal had just two regulation wins, both against Toronto. Watch the assists. Our range has him between 82 and 113 points.
headline: Suzuki is back, and Montreal looks different
